newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to delay entrance at ATPC tin group.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to delay entrance at ATPC tin group.

text.p: Brazil will delay joining the Association of Tin Producing Countries (ATPC) and maintain its observer status on the grounds the organization is too weak, a government official said.
"Our entrance now would be useless," Giovanni Toniatti, secretary of Mines and Metalurgy at the Mines and Energy Ministry, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Last year, at a meeting in Bolivia, Brazilian representatives said the country would join the ATPC. Many observers expected Brazil to join this year.
But Toniatti said Thailand's recent pullout from the ATPC has weakened the association, which seeks to control the world's supply of tin.
The current supply rationalization scheme is not likely to work because only a few members countries are willing to adopt export quotas if world stocks are high, he said.
Last year, Brazilian mining firms produced 15,587 metric tons of tin metal and 17,230 tonnes of tin contained in concentrate, said the country's Tin Industry Union.
In 1996, Brazil is expected to produce 18,000 tonnes of tin metal. Brazil is Latin America's largest tin producer and Paranapanema SA is the country's top tin miner.
